claims.claim: Anthropic launched Claude Ship on 23 November
claims.quote: Publication date: November 23, 2026

claims.claim: Code Review is generally available; PR Steward and Claude Approvals are in public beta
claims.quote: Code Review is generally available. PR Steward and Claude Approvals are in public beta.

claims.claim: Team and Enterprise only, GitHub only, billed on tokens, not available with Zero Data Retention
claims.quote: Claude Ship is available on Claude Team and Enterprise plans for repositories on GitHub. / Claude Ship usage is billed on tokens ... / not available to organizations with Zero Data Retention.

claims.claim: The docs say PR Steward is designed not to approve or merge, but warn that auto-merge or a merge queue with no human requirement can still land a change nobody looked at
claims.quote: Steward is designed not to approve or merge pull requests. / If you use GitHub auto-merge or a merge queue with a policy that doesn't require a person's approval, a change can merge without anyone acting.

claims.claim: Approvals can post an approving review where a policy file in your repo allows it; observe mode exists
claims.quote: You write its policy file, which can set how many people have to approve changes to a path, and where Claude can post an approving review. / Start in observe mode, where the Claude Approvals check reports what your policy would decide. Observe mode is billed.

claims.claim: (share field) Claude Ship has three parts ... billed on tokens; (try-this) baseline is human review time and revert rate
claims.quote: Each agent is billed on token usage through your organization's usage credits. Also unmentioned in the brief: not available with HIPAA configuration or customer-managed encryption keys; PR Steward has no spend limit of its own until you set one.
claims.fix: Accurate as far as it goes. Optionally add that observe mode is billed and PR Steward has no default spend limit; the brief lists only ZDR as an exclusion but docs also exclude HIPAA configuration and customer-managed keys.

claims.claim: 28 layers of the GLM-5 base model reused across two iterations; 1M-token context; 128K max output; first Loop Transformer
claims.quote: reuses 28 layers of the GLM-5 base model across two iterations; context 1M; max output 128K; 'the first built on the Loop Transformer architecture'

claims.claim: Model API arrives 'upon completion of the security assessment'; for now reachable through a Coding Plan
claims.quote: The Model API will be made available upon completion of the security assessment. / GLM-5.4 is now available to all GLM Coding Plan users

claims.claim: Simon Willison notes it isn't open weights, at least not yet
claims.quote: GLM 5.4 is not (yet?) available as open weights.

claims.claim: No weights and no price
claims.quote: Searched the docs page: no pricing figures, no mention of open weights, open source or Hugging Face. Simon Willison: 'not (yet?) available as open weights'; 'I had to sign up for their Coding Plan subscription because 5.4 cannot currently be accessed through the regular API.' Z.ai pricing page not checked.

claims.claim: The trade is clear even without benchmarks; 'until someone publishes numbers you can check'
claims.quote: The page has a win-rate chart (image, no numbers in text) and states: 'average output length drops by 10-14%, mostly from shorter chains of thought' on benchmarks such as GPQA-Diamond and MMLU-Pro. Quota 1.5x that of GLM-5.3 for weekly-quota plans.
claims.fix: Say the docs give no benchmark scores (only a win-rate chart image and a 10-14% drop in average output length), rather than 'without benchmarks'.

claims.claim: More compute per token from the same parameter count, plus the cache design to go with it; Thinking Machines' looped models
claims.quote: the second loop reuses the sparse KV selected in the first pass; an extra loop only costs one sliding window of KV cache rather than a full context cache. Willison: Inkling 2 Mini from Thinking Machines Lab on November 20th is 'a looped transformer'.

claims.claim: At QCon SF, Netflix's Mark Khuzam described rebuilding the SDLC for coding agents, as InfoQ reports
claims.quote: Mark Khuzam, senior software engineer at Netflix; QCon San Francisco 2026; published Nov 23, 2026

claims.claim: 45 ADRs for both people and agents; more than 300 other documents discoverable
claims.quote: The team wrote 45 architecture decision records, each "written for people and for agents." / To keep those records and more than 300 other documents findable

claims.claim: AGENTS.md file in repos "like robots.txt for agents" (in quotation marks)
claims.quote: An AGENTS.md file, the project instructions file that coding agents read before anything else, plays the part of robots.txt.
claims.fix: The quoted words 'like robots.txt for agents' do not appear; InfoQ says AGENTS.md 'plays the part of robots.txt'. Paraphrase without quotation marks or quote the InfoQ wording.

claims.claim: First AI reviewer left 23 comments on one PR; now posts only verified blockers with evidence and the rule they break
claims.quote: Its first version left 23 comments on a single PR ... It now posts only verified blockers, each with evidence, a fix and the ADR rule it breaks.

claims.claim: Developer NPS for the internal framework -3 to +25 over three quarters; 32% more PRs year over year; 'None of this is new...' quote
claims.quote: Developer NPS rose from -3 to +25 over three quarters. / 32% more pull requests year over year. / None of this is new. It's good engineering, built for a new reader.

claims.claim: (share field) Netflix says its agent-ready docs and ADRs took developer NPS from -3 to +25
claims.quote: Developer NPS rose from -3 to +25 over three quarters. (InfoQ reports the rise alongside the whole SDLC rebuild; no statement isolating docs and ADRs as the cause was found.)
claims.fix: Say NPS rose from -3 to +25 over three quarters after the SDLC rebuild, per the speaker; do not attribute the rise to docs and ADRs alone. The main text 'The speaker's own results' is fine.

claims.claim: Result is a vendor/speaker self-report
claims.quote: Results are presented by the speaker (InfoQ conference report); no independent measurement cited.

claims.claim: (event date) preprint PreRun
claims.quote: Submitted on 19 Nov 2026 (v1, Thu, 19 Nov 2026 22:40:56 UTC)

claims.claim: 64 configurations, three launches each
claims.quote: 64 text-generation configurations measured in three separate program launches

claims.claim: Open-weight LLMs underestimated latency by 90-99% on held-out configurations zero-shot
claims.quote: On 16 held-out generation configurations, the open-weight LLMs underestimate latency by 90-99% on average without examples.

claims.claim: Claude's zero-shot error was 4.5 times that of a Random Forest trained on 32 configurations; five examples helped Claude a lot
claims.quote: Claude's zero-shot mean absolute error is 4.5 times that of a Random Forest fit on 32 configurations. / Five labeled examples substantially reduce Claude's generation error (benefit varies by timing target).

claims.claim: Data and pipeline will be open-sourced upon acceptance, so no tool to install yet
claims.quote: We will open-source our data and evaluation pipeline upon acceptance. Searched abstract and Comments field ('25 pages, 2 figures'); no repo link.

claims.claim: Went through twelve public evals and found evidence in eight that the grader failed work that should have passed
claims.quote: In eight of twelve public evals studied, there's evidence the grader failed work that should have passed.

claims.claim: Average pass rate hides a large difference in production; a cheap failure can look efficient on a leaderboard while costing engineers review time
claims.quote: Most evals report average pass rate—this hides a huge difference in production. / Agents that fail or give up often can look cost-effective on a leaderboard while stalling on real work. / token-wise and attention-foolish if an engineer has to spend days reviewing outputs.

claims.claim: (telegram/share) graders fail good work in 8 of 12 evals / Eugene Yan found grader failures in 8 of 12 public evals
claims.quote: there's evidence the grader failed work that should have passed
claims.fix: Source says 'evidence' of grader failure in 8 of 12; say 'evidence of grader failures in 8 of 12 public evals'.

claims.claim: Advisory published on 23 November
claims.quote: published GHSA-wpm4-hgr2-xjwr Nov 23, 2026

claims.claim: Moderate, CVSS 3.1 5.4, no CVE
claims.quote: Severity Moderate; CVSS v3.1 5.4, CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:L/A:L; No known CVE

claims.claim: Affected >=1.80.15, <1.108.0; fixed in 1.108.0; check on by default from 1.108.0
claims.quote: Affected versions >=1.80.15, < 1.108.0; Patched versions 1.108.0; check enabled by default starting in 1.108.0

claims.claim: From 1.100.0 you can turn on general_settings.enforce_fallback_model_access
claims.quote: Versions 1.100.0 through 1.106.x are protected only if general_settings.enforce_fallback_model_access was turned on

claims.claim: Team and key router_settings fallbacks can route requests to models the caller isn't allowed to use
claims.quote: Stored fallbacks were applied after that check, so they were never validated ... router_settings ... can be stored on a key. Team admins (not proxy admins) could use models outside their team's allowed list.

claims.claim: If compromised: not stated in the advisory
claims.quote: Searched the whole advisory: no Patches/Workarounds/Resources/Credits sections, and no mention of compromise, rotation, audit logs or indicators.
